title: harden auth routing for admin and dashboard paths
description: harden auth routing for admin and dashboard paths. The middleware `config.matcher` now includes `/:locale/admin(.*)` and `/:locale/dashboard(.*)`, matching the page entries of `PROTECTED_ROUTE_PATTERNS`, so every request under those trees gets the middleware's sign-in check. The admin and dashboard trees also have server layouts that check the session through `requireAuth()` (Clerk `auth()`) and redirect a signed-out request to `/<locale>/sign-in` with the tree root as `redirect_url` (`lib/protected-page-guard.ts`). Tests: `tests/unit/middleware-matcher-protected-trees.test.ts`, `tests/unit/protected-page-guard.test.ts`

title: the middleware classifies percent-encoded paths
description: the middleware classifies percent-encoded paths. `routeAccess()` matched the raw pathname, which keeps percent escapes, so `/en/%61dmin` and `/api/%61dmin/x` classed as unprotected and skipped the sign-in check; only the router's 404 kept them from serving. A path is now protected when its raw form or its once-decoded form (`decodeURIComponent`, as Next's route lookup does) is protected, and an anonymous request whose raw or decoded path is under `/api/` gets 401. A path is decoded once only, so `/en/%2561dmin` stays unprotected and the router answers 404; a malformed escape such as `%E0%A4%A` classifies the raw path and never throws. Public paths, including `/api/cron/*`, keep their class, and decoding never makes a path public. Tests: `tests/unit/route-access-encoded-228.test.ts` (#228)

title: enforce admin authentication on admin tool-scoring API routes
description: enforce admin authentication on admin tool-scoring API routes. `/api/admin/tools/scoring` (GET/POST/PUT) and `/api/admin/tools/scoring/recalculate` (POST) now call `requireAdmin()` from `lib/api-auth.ts` before any database access: 401 without a session, 403 for a non-admin. The same check replaces the sign-in-only check in the other `/api/admin/*` handlers that had one (articles by id, article recalculate and ingest, articles-v2, db-status, db-status-v2, rankings rollback and versions, SEO sitemap submission, image upload) and is added to the stub handlers that had none. The middleware now checks protected routes (`/:locale/admin`, `/:locale/dashboard`, `/api/admin`) before public ones, anchors public page patterns to a configured locale segment (`lib/route-access.ts`), and answers an anonymous protected `/api/*` request with a 401 JSON body instead of a sign-in redirect

title: /api/data/db-status and /api/data/articles now verify the Clerk session through requireAdmin() instead of checking that…
description: `/api/data/db-status` and `/api/data/articles` now verify the Clerk session through `requireAdmin()` instead of checking that a session cookie is present. An anonymous caller gets 401 and a signed-in non-admin gets 403, with no database details in either response. `lib/manual-auth.ts` and the unused `lib/server-actions/admin-actions.ts`, its only other caller, are removed. The what's-new summary regeneration POST and `/api/ai/analyze-news` also require an admin through `requireAdmin()`. Tests: `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`.

title: requireAdmin() and requireAuth() in lib/api-auth.ts fail closed when NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY or…
description: `requireAdmin()` and `requireAuth()` in `lib/api-auth.ts` fail closed when `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` or `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is missing in a production-like environment (`NODE_ENV=production`, or `VERCEL_ENV` of `production` or `preview`): they return 503 and never a mock user, and `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTH` is ignored there. The mock identities remain for local development only, with a warning. Tests: `tests/unit/api-auth-fail-closed.test.ts`.

title: POST /api/admin/articles/[id]/recalculate runs requireAdmin() before it reads the request body
description: `POST /api/admin/articles/[id]/recalculate` runs `requireAdmin()` before it reads the request body. The middleware answers an anonymous request to a protected API path with 401 regardless of the path's letter case (`/API/admin/...` used to get a sign-in redirect). `tests/unit/middleware-route-access.test.ts` now checks the exported `config.matcher` with Next's `unstable_doesMiddlewareMatch`, including bare `/api/admin`, `.json` and `.png` suffixes, an upper-case path and Clerk sign-in sub-routes.

title: the public GET /api/whats-new/summary only reads stored summaries and never starts generation
description: the public `GET /api/whats-new/summary` only reads stored summaries and never starts generation. Without a `period` it serves the current month's stored summary, else the most recent stored one; otherwise it returns 404. Generation runs only through the admin POST. `/api/data(.*)` and `/api/ai(.*)` join the middleware's protected routes, so an anonymous request is refused before the handler runs. `/api/data/db-status` reports a masked host (a short first-label prefix plus `***`) instead of the full hostname. Tests: `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`, `tests/unit/middleware-route-access.test.ts`.

title: article ingestion no longer deletes the stored what's-new summary, so a summary persists until an admin regenerates it…
description: article ingestion no longer deletes the stored what's-new summary, so a summary persists until an admin regenerates it (automatic regeneration: #160), and the empty-state copy no longer promises automatic generation. `POST /api/companies` requires an admin through `requireAdmin()`; the list GET stays public. The admin dashboard page and `GET /api/admin/articles` use `requireAdmin()`, and `lib/auth-helper.ts`, which returned a mock admin whenever `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISABLE_AUTH` was set, is removed with the unused `lib/clerk-auth.ts`. The `/api/admin` debug routes (`debug-auth`, `test-auth`, `runtime-fix-test`, `db-test`, `bypass-test`) keep their production 404 and otherwise require an admin. The auth helpers bypass Clerk only when `NODE_ENV` is `development` or `test` and `VERCEL_ENV` is unset or `development`. `/api/data/db-status` reports a fixed `connectionError` string. Tests: `tests/unit/ingestion-keeps-summary.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-page-debug-routes-auth.test.ts`, `tests/unit/auth-hardening.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-api-auth.test.ts`, `tests/unit/api-auth-fail-closed.test.ts`.

title: migration 0022_fix_grok_stray_kind.sql gives the grok-4-5, grok-4-6 and grok-4-7 rows kind model and archives them…
description: migration `0022_fix_grok_stray_kind.sql` gives the `grok-4-5`, `grok-4-6` and `grok-4-7` rows kind `model` and archives them (owner ruling D7b). The rows held the 0016 default kind `harness` with status `pending_review`, so the model seed refused `grok-4-5` and `grok-4-6`, and its status step refuses a `pending_review` row. The migration sets `kind = 'model'`, `subcategory = NULL` and `status = 'deprecated'` on all three and records `data.d7b.supersededBy = 'grok'`; `grok-4-7` duplicates the live `grok` row (Grok 4.7). The seed's status step then moves `grok-4-5` and `grok-4-6` from deprecated to deprecated and adds its lifecycle record. One DO block: it raises and writes nothing unless all three rows exist as `harness`/`pending_review`, no `tool_links` row touches them, and `grok` is an active model. A re-run is a no-op, and a partial state raises. Tests: `tests/unit/grok-kind-fix-d7b.test.ts` (#329)

title: the home page top-3 card titles are readable in the narrow three-column layout (about 900 px)
description: the home page top-3 card titles are readable in the narrow three-column layout (about 900 px). The title has its own full-width row in a fixed two-line slot, so names wrap instead of being cut to one letter, and a name that needs more than two lines ends in an ellipsis with the full name in a tooltip. The rank pill and trend arrow sit on the logo row and stay inside the card, and the "SWE-bench" label no longer wraps. Cards keep equal heights and aligned rows. Tests: `tests/unit/hero-card-323.test.tsx` (#326)

title: the home page top-3 cards line up
description: the home page top-3 cards line up. The three cards have equal height, the #1 card keeps a ring highlight without being scaled, and its "#1 Ranked" badge has a visible background. Logo, title and rank pill sit at the same height on every card, descriptions take three lines, and the Score / SWE-bench row sits at the card bottom with an em dash for a missing SWE-bench value. The header nav links share the header's centre line with the "Last updated" pill and the right-side controls. Tests: `tests/unit/hero-card-323.test.tsx` (#323)

title: the models list is no longer topped by a retired tool, ties rank in slug order, and the list is noindex
description: the models list is no longer topped by a retired tool, ties rank in slug order, and the list is noindex. A per-list board built from the combined board (`loadCurrentRankings()`, read by `/<locale>/rankings/<list>` and `/api/rankings?list=`) now drops rows whose tool is not `active` (for example `redirect`) and renumbers ranks, tiers and previous ranks from 1; the stored ranking data is not changed, and `/api/rankings/current` does not use this reader. `loadActiveTools()` orders by slug, so tools with equal scores rank in slug order instead of database read order; no scoring factor, weight or tie rule changed. The models list is noindex at any size (`NOINDEX_LISTS` in `lib/rankings/lists.ts`, `list_meta.indexable` false, left out of the sitemap) and its page shows a note in all 10 locales (`rankings.lists.modelsMetricsPendingNote`) that the order is provisional because model metrics are not collected yet. The harness and productivity lists keep the 10-entry indexing rule (D53). Tests: `tests/unit/ranking-tie-order-slug.test.ts`, `tests/unit/models-list-inactive-rows.test.ts`, `tests/unit/models-list-noindex.test.tsx`

title: a tool write that matches no row now fails instead of reporting success
description: a tool write that matches no row now fails instead of reporting success. `ToolsRepository.deleteById` and `updateScoring` matched `data->>'id'`, so a row with no `data.id` was never deleted or scored, and `deleteById` still returned true. Both now find the row through `findById` and write it by its UUID `id`; `deleteById` returns false and `updateScoring` returns null when no row is written. `findById` and `findByIds` no longer compare a non-UUID id to the uuid column, which made Postgres throw and the admin routes answer 500; a non-UUID id matches only a legacy `data.id`, else the lookup is not found. In `/api/admin/tools`, `refresh-display` and `update-company` answer 404 when the update writes no row, `DELETE ?id=` answers 404 instead of 500 when the delete removes no row, the `delete` action answers 404 when it deleted nothing, `cleanup-auto` lists a delete that removed no row under `errors`, and `quick-fix-display` and `update-missing-company` count only updates that wrote a row and list the rest in `failedTools`. `findByIds` binds its legacy `data.id` lookup ids as parameters instead of splicing them into SQL text. Tests: `tests/unit/tool-repo-writes-290.test.ts` (#290)

title: GET /api/rankings takes a required request: Request
description: `GET /api/rankings` takes a required `request: Request`. #279 declared it `request?: Request`, which `next build` rejects as an invalid route export, so the production build failed. A request with no `list` parameter still returns the coding-harness board (D51). Tests: `tests/unit/rankings-per-list-read-186.test.ts`, `tests/unit/home-live-rankings-192.test.tsx` (#186)

title: the github metrics collector runs without GITHUB_TOKEN (owner ruling A9e)
description: the github metrics collector runs without `GITHUB_TOKEN` (owner ruling A9e). It no longer throws "GITHUB_TOKEN is not set", sends no `Authorization` header, and reads repo metadata only (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}`); `commit_count_30d` and `contributors_count` are not collected, so they are absent from `tool_metrics_history`, not stored as 0. With a token the commit and contributor calls still run. Any 403 or 429 (including `Retry-After`) now fails that tool instead of storing a 0. Rate-limit state is read from `x-ratelimit-*` response headers, and when the remaining budget is below what a tool needs the shard stops fetching: the unreached tools count as skipped (in `skipped_timeout`), the shard status is `partial`, and the stop reason is written to the `metrics_collection_runs.error` column (#95)

title: the Tools Manager's edit and discontinue actions answered 405
description: the Tools Manager's edit and discontinue actions answered 405. The hook sent PUT and DELETE to the public `/api/tools/[slug]/json`, which serves GET only. They now go to `PUT` and `DELETE /api/admin/tools/[slug]`, which call `requireAdmin()` before reading the body or the database: 401 without a session, 403 for a non-admin. PUT edits `name`, `category`, `status` (active, inactive, deprecated or discontinued) and `description`, refuses any other key or an empty edit with 400, and answers 404 for an unknown slug. DELETE discontinues the tool: it sets the status to `discontinued` and keeps the row and its history (the hard delete stays `DELETE /api/admin/tools?id=`). The confirm dialog now says Discontinue. The hook changes its list only when a 2xx answer carries the written row, mapped through `toManagerTool`; any other answer rejects with the server's error. `ToolsRepository.update` writes `name`, `category`, `status` and `slug` to the JSONB as well as the columns, so a stale `data.status` no longer hides a status change, and it updates the row by UUID, so a row with no `data.id` can be edited. The same change makes the admin bulk actions `refresh-display`, `update-company`, `quick-fix-display` and `update-missing-company` take effect on tool rows that have no `data.id`; before, their update matched no row, so they did nothing. Tests: `tests/unit/admin-tool-edit-288.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-tool-edit-hook-288.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/admin-tools-list-197.test.tsx` (#288)

title: /api/tools leaves out every tool whose slug the signed #191 URL table marks noindex (isNoindexToolSlug in…
description: `/api/tools` leaves out every tool whose slug the signed #191 URL table marks noindex (`isNoindexToolSlug` in `lib/seo/url-table.ts`), so `/<locale>/tools` and its search no longer list the non-AI entities such as `anthropic`, `aws` or `stripe`. Each such tool's own page still answers 200 with `noindex, nofollow`, and `/api/tools/[slug]/json` still returns it. The list is filtered before it is cached, under a new in-memory cache key. The "Total tools" figure that the home and rankings pages count from `/api/tools` now counts listed tools only; ranked rows, ranks and scores are unchanged. Tests: `tests/unit/tools-route-noindex-197.test.ts` (#197)

title: admin rankings readers and writers handle bare-array snapshot rows
description: admin rankings readers and writers handle bare-array snapshot rows. The cron and admin-draft writers store `rankings.data` as a bare array, so `GET`/`PUT /api/admin/rankings/[period]`, `/api/admin/rankings/periods`, `/api/admin/check-ranking-periods` and the `periods`, `check-data`, `all` and `sync-current` actions of `/api/admin/rankings` reported 0 rows for those rows, and `check-data` reported `has_scores: false`. They now read rows through `snapshotRows()` (`lib/rankings/snapshot-rows.ts`), which accepts a bare array, `{ rankings }` or `{ data }`, and returns [] for null or malformed data; `has_scores` is false when a period has no rows. `PUT` with no `rankings` in the body keeps the stored rows instead of writing `{ rankings: [] }`, and a non-array `rankings` gets 400. `sync-current` writes `public/data/rankings.json` and the static cache as `{ ...fields, rankings: [...], is_current: true }` instead of spreading the array into numeric keys, and `set-current` writes `public/data/rankings.json` the same way. `create-period` with `copy_from` copies a bare source's rows and keeps its `algorithm_version`. `PUT` with no `rankings` and `sync-current` return 409 and write nothing when the stored data has no readable rows (for example a numeric-key object); an empty `[]` or `{ rankings: [] }` row still updates and syncs. Article ingestion reads the current row's rankings the same way. Tests: `tests/unit/admin-rankings-bare-array-256.test.ts` (#256)

title: the home page movers strip lists the biggest rank changes
description: the home page movers strip lists the biggest rank changes. The "Trending Tools" strip was filled in client effects only, read the first 30 ranks, took the first 3 risers in rank order, never listed a faller, and showed the top 3 tools under "Tools gaining momentum this week" when no tool moved. It is now "Biggest movers", labelled "Since last update" (with the snapshot date when one is given) instead of a week: up to 3 risers and 3 fallers, each with a signed delta, chosen from every rank by size of move, then better current rank, then name (`lib/rankings/select-movers.ts`). A row with no previous rank is not a mover. With no movers the strip shows one line and no tool names. It renders from the rows the server passes, so it is in the server HTML; the labels are new `home.movers` keys in every locale. The home page read a hardcoded three-row list ("Algorithm v7.6 rankings (November 2025)") with no rank changes, so its top 3 was stale and the strip was always empty. It now reads the current published snapshot on the server through `loadCurrentRankings()` in `lib/rankings/current-rankings.ts`, which `/api/rankings` also uses, so both show the same rows, ranks and rank changes; the strip's date is the snapshot's `published_at` (else `created_at`). When the read fails or no snapshot is current, the page still renders, logs a warning and shows the empty state with no tool names. The client-side rankings fetch and its `public/data/rankings.json` fallback are removed. `/rankings` and the `/api/rankings` response shape are unchanged. Tests: `lib/rankings/select-movers.test.ts`, `tests/unit/home-movers-192.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/home-live-rankings-192.test.tsx` (#192)

title: an article's primary tool follows mention relevance
description: an article's primary tool follows mention relevance. The primary tool was the first stored mention that resolved to a catalogue tool, so when an article's subject is not in the catalogue a passing mention became its tool: "Manus Secures $500M Funding" (Manus at relevance 1) was attributed to Cursor through a 0.3 competitor mention and listed on the Cursor page. Now only the mentions with the highest relevance compete, ties go to stored order, and when none of them resolves the article has no primary tool, even if a weaker mention resolves. A mention without a relevance ranks below every scored one. The title is read for a primary tool only when an article has no mentions. `/api/news` `tool_slug`, `/api/news/[slug]` `tool` and the tool page's Related news all read `primaryArticleTool` in `lib/news-tool-resolver.ts`, so they agree. `tool_name` still lists every resolved tool; response shapes are unchanged. On the 100 newest live articles, 64 keep a primary tool instead of 84: 20 lose it and 5 change tool. Attribution feeds no ranking score or publish path. Tests: `tests/unit/news-primary-tool-109.test.ts`, `tests/unit/news-route-tools-109.test.ts` (#109)

title: /<locale>/tools/<slug> answers 404 when no tool in the catalogue has that slug
description: `/<locale>/tools/<slug>` answers 404 when no tool in the catalogue has that slug. The page rendered for any slug, so an unknown one answered 200 with a client-side "Tool Not Found" text and no canonical. The page now calls `notFound()` when the catalogue lookup returns no row; a tool in any status (active, pending_review, inactive) renders as before, and a failed lookup throws to the error page (5xx) instead of rendering. The 404 page is noindex and has a search box held in client state (no form, no `name`; it sends `site_search` with `search_location: "tool_not_found"`), up to five links to the nearest active tools by edit distance (`lib/tools/nearest-tools.ts`), and a link to the rankings. The generic not-found page uses the design-system Card and Button and `--ds-*` classes instead of inline styles and hex colours, and the colour ratchet now covers it. Tests: `tests/unit/tool-not-found-193.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/analytics-events.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/globals-consolidation-189.test.ts` (#193)

title: news articles are attributed to tools in the tool catalogue
description: news articles are attributed to tools in the tool catalogue. `/api/news` read `mention.tool` while stored mentions carry `name` and `toolId`, so every item showed "Various Tools" with no `tool_slug`; both news routes also matched titles against a hand-kept list of 15 coarse slugs (`claude`, `gemini`, `replit-ai`) that are not in the catalogue, and `/api/news/[slug]` ignored `toolId`. Both routes now resolve through `lib/news-tool-resolver.ts`: a mention's `toolId`, then a mention name equal to a catalogue name or slug, then catalogue names found in the title as whole words, with no fuzzy or partial matching. Title matching uses names only, never slugs, and is case-sensitive; a name that is a single all-letter word (such as Continue, Warp or AI) is never matched in a title and is attributed through mentions only. A returned slug is always a catalogue slug. The catalogue is read once per request and cached in memory for 5 minutes (`lib/news-tool-catalogue.ts`); when the read fails, both routes still answer 200 with no attribution and log one warning. `lib/tool-matcher.ts` and its tests are removed. Response shapes are unchanged. Tests: `tests/unit/news-tool-resolver-109.test.ts`, `tests/unit/news-route-tools-109.test.ts` (#109)

title: a tool whose info.company or info.company_name is an object, a number or true no longer aborts the ranking run
description: a tool whose `info.company` or `info.company_name` is an object, a number or `true` no longer aborts the ranking run. The engine called `.includes` on the value, which threw a TypeError in `calculateCompanyBacking` and stopped `computeRankings()`, including the monthly cron. Such a value now scores exactly as an absent field, in both company backing and data completeness, and the engine logs one warning per affected tool with the tool id and the type found. Every value that did not throw scores as before, including strings and arrays; the algorithm version stays v7.9. The field mapping for the other `info.*` fields is in `docs/algorithms/info-field-mapping.md`. Tests: `lib/ranking-algorithm-v76.company-guard.test.ts` (#241)

title: article pages showed the previous day in browsers west of UTC, and React threw hydration error #418
description: article pages showed the previous day in browsers west of UTC, and React threw hydration error #418. An article dated `2026-10-21T00:00:00Z` rendered "October 20, 2026" in America/Los_Angeles while the server rendered "October 21, 2026". Client components now format stored UTC dates with `formatUtcDate()` in `lib/format-utc-date.ts`, which forces `timeZone: "UTC"`: the news article header, the news list and news card dates (whose year check now uses the UTC year), the home news card, the rankings "last updated" and "Rankings as of" dates, and the What's New modal month and generated date. Formats and relative labels ("2 days ago") are unchanged. Tests: `tests/unit/utc-client-dates-239.test.tsx` (#239)

title: /<locale>/whats-new showed "No Monthly Summary Available" while a summary was stored
description: `/<locale>/whats-new` showed "No Monthly Summary Available" while a summary was stored. The server component fetched the relative URL `/api/whats-new/summary`; a server-side `fetch` cannot resolve a relative URL, so the read rejected and the error was swallowed. The page now reads the latest stored summary through the summary service. The empty state appears only when no summary is stored, and a failed database read shows the error page. Month and generation dates are formatted in UTC, so a server west of UTC no longer names the previous month. Tests: `tests/unit/whats-new-permalink.test.ts` (#54)

title: the ingestion gap check reported the 06:00 UTC daily run four hours late when run outside UTC
description: the ingestion gap check reported the 06:00 UTC daily run four hours late when run outside UTC. The `timestamp` columns hold UTC with no zone, and the database driver read them in the process time zone. Raw SQL readers in `scripts/` now parse them as UTC through `lib/db/naive-utc-timestamp.mjs` (`naiveUtcTypes`, `parseNaiveUtcTimestamp`) or `getRawSql()` in `lib/db/connection.ts`, so the gap, age and printed times match under any `TZ`. No schema change. `docs/deployment/cron-schedules-and-timestamps.md` records that `vercel.json` crons run on UTC. Tests: `tests/unit/naive-utc-timestamp.test.ts`, `tests/unit/naive-utc-timestamp-tz.test.ts` (#103)

title: the What's New feed and /api/changelog showed no platform changes in production
description: the What's New feed and `/api/changelog` showed no platform changes in production. `.vercelignore` matched `/*.md`, so the deploy dropped CHANGELOG.md, and `/api/changelog` answered `200 []` with no error. `npm run build` now compiles CHANGELOG.md into `data/changelog-entries.generated.json` (`npm run generate-changelog`), and the runtime imports it instead of reading the file. `[Unreleased]` entries are shown, each dated by the commit that introduced its line (the build date when none resolves). `/api/whats-new` reads these entries instead of a hardcoded 2025-10 list and holds 3 of its 20 slots for them. Both routes report `_sources` and `_degraded`; an empty module makes `/api/changelog` answer 503 instead of `200 []`. `.vercelignore` keeps CHANGELOG.md, and the `outputFileTracingIncludes` entries for it are removed. A sync test fails when the generated module is stale (#231)

title: rankings search terms no longer reach a URL or GA4 page_location
description: rankings search terms no longer reach a URL or GA4 `page_location`. The middleware answers a page GET or HEAD carrying `term`, `search`, `q`, `s`, `query` or `keyword` with a 308 to the same URL without those keys, before the auth checks; `/api` and `/_next` are untouched (`lib/search-url-keys.ts`). The rankings grid has a search box held in client state (no form, no `name`), and its badge clears the box without navigating. `site_search` fires once per settled term, 800 ms after typing stops. The schema.org SearchAction is removed from the home page and both JSON-LD builders, and `lib/search-param.ts` is deleted. Tests: `tests/unit/search-term-redaction-233.test.ts`, `tests/unit/analytics-events.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/seo-canonical-origin.test.ts` (#233)

title: /<locale>/whats-new/recent always showed the "Error / Try Again" card in production although /api/whats-new?days=7…
description: `/<locale>/whats-new/recent` always showed the "Error / Try Again" card in production although `/api/whats-new?days=7` returned items. The page built its server-side feed URL from `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, falling back to `http://localhost:3000`; the variable is unset in production, so the read went to localhost and failed. The page now builds the URL from `siteOrigin()` in `lib/site-origin.ts`. A failed read still renders the error card and an empty feed still renders "No Recent Updates" (#152) (#219)

title: two GA4 defects from the production collect capture
description: two GA4 defects from the production collect capture. (1) The rankings sort select and the sidebar feature-tag buttons sent `filter_use` and then set `window.location.href`, a full document load. gtag.js holds a hit for about five seconds before sending it, so that hit could only leave in the pagehide flush, which the capture never saw. Both controls now navigate with the App Router (`router.push`), as the sidebar category links and the `/tools` selects already did, so the page stays loaded and gtag sends the hit from its normal batch. The URL, the sort and the filter results are unchanged. (2) The rankings search term was in the `search` query key, one of the keys GA4 enhanced measurement reads as a site search, so the raw term reached GA4 as `view_search_results.search_term`. The key is now `term` (`lib/search-param.ts`) in both schema.org SearchActions (home page and root layout); the rankings page reads `term` first and still accepts `?search=` from old links, and the search badge clears both. No custom event changes name or parameters. The raw term is still in the `page_view` URL. Tests: `tests/unit/analytics-filter-delivery.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/analytics-events.test.tsx`, `tests/unit/seo-canonical-origin.test.ts` (#175)

title: /<locale>/unauthorized answers 200 instead of 500
description: `/<locale>/unauthorized` answers 200 instead of 500. The page is a Server Component and passed an `onClick` handler to its "Go Back" button, which React cannot send to the browser, so every render threw. The button is now a client component (`app/[lang]/(authenticated)/unauthorized/go-back-button.tsx`). The middleware also classes `/<locale>/unauthorized` as public (`lib/route-access.ts`), so the static page no longer triggers a session lookup; no other route changes class. title: the quality assessment step failed open
description: the quality assessment step failed open. An unparseable reply fell back to default scores with no error, so the candidate was counted as `quality_rejected` and a run in which no reply parsed still ended `completed` with a 200. An unparseable reply now yields an assessment carrying `error`, logged at error level, and the candidate is recorded as `assessment_failed`; replies are parsed with the shared `extractJsonObject()`. When every assessed candidate fails assessment, the run ends `failed` and `/api/cron/daily-news` answers 500.
